sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Osceola County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Deeds for Osceola County property are recorded at the Register of Deeds on the first floor of the main courthouse, 301 W. Upton Avenue, Reed City, MI 49677. The office phone is (231) 832-6113, the fax is (231) 832-6115, and the email is register@osceolacountymi.gov. Hours run Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm except holidays, and the public computer terminals are open until 4:45 pm.

Reed City has been the county seat since 1927. When Osceola County organized its own government in 1869 the seat was Hersey, and the move to Reed City came decades later. The register's land records reach back to 1853, which is older than the county's separate government, because the territory was attached to other counties for administration before 1869.

The office is the official recording office for real estate documents, keeps the permanent land records, maintains a full tract index by legal description for every parcel in the county, and chairs the county Plat Board. It does not prepare documents or answer legal questions, so a seller who needs a deed drafted should use an attorney or a title company.

sections.h2: What does the Osceola County Register of Deeds charge?
sections.html:
The base charge is $30 per document, no matter how many pages it has. The county cites MCL 600.2567(1)(a) for that figure, and the same section sets the copy and certification fees below. The office takes cash, credit cards, checks and money orders, and makes payment out to Register of Deeds; card processing adds a separate charge.

The county treasurer's tax certification fee can be folded into one payment made to the Register of Deeds, so a seller or title agent does not need a second check for a warranty deed.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies to an Osceola County sale?
sections.html:
Osceola County posts its two transfer taxes per thousand dollars of value: $1.10 for the county and $7.50 for the state. The state share comes from MCL 207.525 at $3.75 per $500, and the county share comes from MCL 207.504 at 55 cents per $500 in a county with fewer than 2,000,000 residents. Both apply to each $500 or fraction of it.

On a $150,000 sale, a figure near the county's $155,400 median home value, the math is 300 units of $500. That gives $1,125 for the state and $165 for the county, or $1,290 in all. A deed has to show the full value on its face, or an affidavit of value must be attached. In a sale that bundles real and personal property, only the real property is taxed when the two values are stated separately.

Some transfers escape one tax and not the other, and the lists differ. These are the points most relevant to a house seller:

  • A deed given for consideration under $100 is exempt under both acts.
  • A deed given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a government-backed loan is exempt under both acts, and the state act also covers mortgage foreclosures generally.
  • A conveyance from a parent to a child or from a grandparent to a grandchild is exempt under the state act, MCL 207.526. The county list in MCL 207.505 has no family exemption.
  • A court order that makes a transfer without setting a price is exempt under both acts.
  • A land contract is exempt until legal title passes at full payment.

The exemption must be written on the face of the deed. Ask the Register of Deeds at (231) 832-6113 how the office wants it worded before you sign.

sections.h2: What must a deed meet before Osceola County will accept it?
sections.html:
The register can refuse a deed that breaks the format rules in MCL 565.201, so check these items before you leave the closing table:

  • A top margin of at least 2.5 inches on the first page and half an inch on every other side.
  • Black ink on white paper of at least 20-pound weight, in 10-point type or larger, sized between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Each signer's name printed beneath the signature, matching the name in the notary acknowledgment.
  • The grantee's street address, and the name and business address of whoever drafted the document.
  • At least the first five digits of any Social Security number hidden, plus an English translation if any part is in another language.

Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts also need a tax certificate from the county treasurer, according to the county's fee page. MCL 211.135 backs this up: the certificate shows whether tax liens exist and whether taxes for the five years before the instrument are paid. A quitclaim deed with no covenants of warranty is excused from that step.

sections.h2: How do I search Osceola County land records before a sale?
sections.html:
Land records are searchable online from 1988 to the present through the county's Online Land Records Search, and each document is imaged so it can be pulled by liber and page. Older entries sit in handwritten grantor and grantee index books that run through 2003, and the public terminals in the courthouse cover names from 1988 forward. Browsing the name indexes costs nothing.

The handwritten tract index runs from 1853 to the present. Searching it by legal description costs $50 per hour, a rate the Board of Commissioners set. Staff do not run title or mineral searches. Written search requests are finished as time allows, with a goal of three days, so a seller who needs a same-day answer should call a title company.

The register's page also offers Fraud Notify. You enter your name and email, and the office alerts you when a document is recorded under that name. An owner who plans to sell a vacant or inherited house can use it to catch a forged deed early. The same page links to the county's GIS parcel maps.

sections.h2: What should I know about selling a house in Osceola County?
sections.html:
Osceola County covers 573 square miles of rolling, once fully wooded land in Northern Michigan. Reed City and Evart are the two cities, and the villages are Hersey, LeRoy, Marion and Tustin. US 10 and US 131 cross the county, along with M-61, M-66 and M-115. The county began as Unwattin County in 1840 and took the Osceola name in 1843, and lumbering drew its first wave of settlers.

The Census Bureau counts 22,891 people in the 2020 census and estimates 23,516 for July 2025. For 2020 to 2024 it lists a median owner-occupied home value of $155,400 and an owner-occupied rate of 83.7%. Median gross rent is $807 a month, and median household income is $58,267. The same release shows zero building permits issued in 2025 and about 12,756 housing units, a thin permit record that leaves most listings as older homes.

The county's website carried a notice about flooding from April 10 to 21, 2026, with a fact sheet on U.S. Small Business Administration disaster loans. An owner whose house took water should read it before pricing a sale.

Unpaid taxes matter at closing, because a warranty deed will not record without the treasurer's certificate. Ask the Osceola County Treasurer for a current payoff figure before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Is the Osceola County recording fee based on page count?
faqs.a: No. The fee is $30 per document regardless of the number of pages, under MCL 600.2567(1)(a), with $3 added for each extra instrument that a single document assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: Can I email a recorded deed from the Osceola County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's fee page lists a $7.00 charge for sending documents by email. Copies at the counter are $1.00 per page, and a certified copy costs $5.00 more.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need a tax certificate in Osceola County?
faqs.a: Generally not. The county page names warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of land contracts as the documents that need the treasurer's certificate, and MCL 211.135 excuses conveyances without covenants of warranty.

faqs.q: What is the Osceola County transfer tax on a $200,000 house?
faqs.a: It is $1,720. The state share is $1,500 at $3.75 per $500 and the county share is $220 at 55 cents per $500, and the deed must state the value or carry an affidavit.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a document I already recorded in Osceola County?
faqs.a: Call the Register of Deeds at (231) 832-6113 or write to register@osceolacountymi.gov. The office is open Monday to Friday from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm except holidays.
